programs.title: Lost Treasures of Egypt: Four Queens Compilation
programs.desc: In ancient Egypt, royal power was reserved for men, but over the centuries, women also sat on the throne.Some ruled as queens, others were crowned pharaoh.The figures of Cleopatra and Nefertiti still exist in popular culture today.The former, due to her alliances with Julius Caesar and Mark Antony, was remembered as an ambitious ruler of extraordinary beauty who excelled in the role of a politician and strategist.Her dramatic fate and suicide death have fired up the imagination of subsequent generations for over two thousand years.The authors will also talk about other extraordinary Egyptian women.Viewers will learn the fate of Hatshepsut, who was the longest-reigning female pharaoh, and Nefertari, the influential wife of Ramesses II.All of them went down in the history of this highly developed civilization.The creators will explain how they reached for titles and power.

programs.title: The Spying Game: Tales from the Cold War
programs.desc: The creators of the program talk about operations undertaken during the Cold War by intelligence officers of the United States of America, the Soviet Union and other countries.

programs.title: Goulag: Une histoire soviétique
programs.desc: Millions of people were sent to forced labor camps in the USSR, including many Poles.Often their fate remained unknown.Not only criminals were sent there, but also political opponents and citizens who offended the system.Cheap labor in mines, quarries and logging was to support the economy.All documents have not yet been declassified.Knowledge about labor camps can be derived, among others, from literature - "The Gulag Archipelago" by Alexander Solzhenitsyn or "Another World" by Gustaw Herling-Grudziński.
